  "title": "VQ-Perceiver World-State Bottleneck for Camera-Viewpoint-Robust Action in MoT WAMs",
  "core_problem": "Motus (Tri-model Joint Attention; WAN2.2-5B + Qwen3-VL-2B + action expert, ~7B total; public weights at motus-robotics/Motus on HuggingFace) achieves 87.0% on the unperturbed split of RoboTwin 2.0-Plus (overall average 71.5%) but drops to 21.6% under camera viewpoint perturbation and 43.1% under sensor noise — a 65 percentage-point camera degradation confirmed in arXiv:2603.22078, Table 3. Critically, appearance perturbations cause minimal degradation: lighting 84.6%, background 84.4%, robot initial state 85.0%. The prior proposal's appearance-robustness framing was empirically wrong: the actual published data shows Motus is resilient to lighting and background but catastrophically fragile under camera viewpoint changes. The camera-viewpoint failure implicates Motus's Tri-model Joint Attention design: action tokens jointly attend to raw video tokens in shared self-attention at every transformer layer, so action predictions are directly conditioned on viewpoint-specific pixel spatial arrangements (perspective projections, egocentric depth layout) encoded in those tokens, rather than viewpoint-invariant semantic state (object pose relative to gripper, task phase, contact configuration). When camera position changes, the spatial distribution of video tokens shifts, breaking the learned visual-to-action correlation. Motus's 21.6% is the most severe camera-viewpoint score among all WAMs evaluated in arXiv:2603.22078; LingBot-VA scores 28.9% on RoboTwin 2.0-Plus camera and Cosmos-Policy scores 75.8% on LIBERO-Plus camera, suggesting scale of video pretraining partially mitigates the issue but does not solve it. Motus was included in RoboTwin 2.0-Plus Table 3 results of arXiv:2603.22078 despite being excluded from the paper's WAM taxonomy discussion (its hybrid VLM-action routing architecture places it outside the strict definition), making it the only publicly-weighted MoT WAM with confirmed, severe camera-viewpoint vulnerability available for fine-tuning studies. IMPORTANT EVALUATION NOTE: RoboTwin 2.0-Plus is an in-house benchmark constructed by Huawei/UToronto for arXiv:2603.22078 — no public evaluation code, GitHub repository, or formal camera perturbation parameter specification has been released; the official RoboTwin 2.0 repo (github.com/RoboTwin-Platform/RoboTwin) applies only minor camera jitter (~1 cm) and does not include the viewpoint-pose perturbation measured in 2603.22078. Accordingly, the 21.6% Motus camera score is cited as published motivation for the problem, but RoboTwin 2.0-Plus is designated a secondary evaluation target contingent on author code release or Appendix A re-implementation. LIBERO-Plus (arXiv:2510.13626) is the primary evaluation benchmark: it is fully public, with evaluation code at github.com/sylvestf/LIBERO-plus and dataset at huggingface.co/datasets/Sylvest/LIBERO-plus, defining three camera sub-axes (C1: distance 1.01×–2.00×; C2: spherical position Δθ/Δϕ within 15°–75° cones; C3: orientation yaw/pitch/roll within 2°–10°), and the current camera-axis SOTA among architecturally-motivated methods trained without camera-augmented demonstrations is OA-WAM at 80.5% (arXiv:2605.06481, Table 2); the LIBERO-Plus benchmark paper itself demonstrates that fine-tuning OpenVLA-OFT on 20,000+ camera-augmented trajectories reaches 92.8%, establishing a data-augmentation ceiling — a distinct setting from the architectural robustness problem addressed here. LIBERO-PLUS BASELINE NOTE: Motus is absent from arXiv:2603.22078's LIBERO-Plus evaluation table — independently confirmed; only RoboTwin 2.0-Plus results appear for Motus in that paper. Zero published data points exist for Motus's LIBERO-Plus camera performance, making the 4h baseline run (day 1–2) a prerequisite for validating the paper's core premise, not merely a calibration step. Crucially, RoboTwin 2.0-Plus and LIBERO-Plus camera scores are not necessarily correlated: Cosmos-Policy achieves 75.8% camera on LIBERO-Plus but a lower score on RoboTwin 2.0-Plus camera, indicating the two benchmarks probe different aspects of viewpoint sensitivity. Motus's LIBERO-Plus camera score could plausibly range from ~55% to ~80%, spanning three qualitatively different contribution scenarios that each require a different paper framing — these scenarios are explicitly defined in the opportunity section.",
  "opportunity": "The gap: camera viewpoint is Motus's specific, quantified Achilles heel (87.0% unperturbed → 21.6% camera-perturbed on RoboTwin 2.0-Plus, per arXiv:2603.22078). The closest prior work, ReViWo (ICLR 2025), establishes the VQ-for-viewpoint-invariance principle in robotic manipulation: it decomposes visual observations into a VQ-coded view-invariant representation (VIR) and a continuous view-dependent representation (VDR), then trains a COMBO-based world model exclusively on VIR to achieve camera-robust control. This is directly related to our proposal — but four constraints make ReViWo inapplicable to our setting: (a) it requires multi-view training data with known camera labels, collected from MetaWorld simulators; (b) it operates on small-scale COMBO/RSSM world models evaluated on MetaWorld and PandaGym tasks; (c) it applies VQ as an offline preprocessing step external to the policy, not inside the running model; (d) it uses model-based RL, not diffusion-based imitation learning. Our contribution extends the VQ-for-viewpoint-invariance principle to a setting that drops all four constraints: a 7B diffusion-based MoT WAM fine-tuned on single-view demonstrations via intra-model cross-attention routing, evaluated on large-scale benchmarks (LIBERO-Plus primary, RoboTwin 2.0-Plus secondary) with a confirmed, quantified 65pp camera vulnerability on RoboTwin 2.0-Plus. No concurrent work applies intra-model VQ routing within a deployed large-scale diffusion WAM without multi-view training data.\n\nARCHITECTURAL VS. DATA-AUGMENTATION MOTIVATION: Camera-augmented fine-tuning is a known alternative — the LIBERO-Plus benchmark paper (arXiv:2510.13626) demonstrates that fine-tuning OpenVLA-OFT on 20,000+ trajectories with systematic camera-view augmentation achieves 92.8% camera robustness on LIBERO-Plus. However, this result carries a material hardware confound: OpenVLA-OFT uses a dual-camera setup (external third-person + wrist camera), where the wrist-mounted camera provides stable close-range geometric cues invariant to external viewpoint changes (confirmed by the LIBERO-Plus paper's own 'third-camera-blinded' ablation); Motus and VQ-Perceiver operate from a single external camera only, addressing a strictly harder single-camera setting — OpenVLA-OFT with dual cameras but without additional fine-tuning achieves only 56.4% camera on LIBERO-Plus. However, this approach has three critical limitations that motivate VQ-Perceiver as a complementary architectural solution. First, the LIBERO-Plus augmentation is calibrated to the test distribution: training uses camera-view shifts within 5° of the test camera positions on spherical coordinates, meaning the approach achieves high performance partly because training covers positions near the test viewpoints — generalization to truly novel, out-of-distribution camera configurations is not established. Second, data collection at scale is infeasible in many deployment scenarios: collecting 20,000+ diverse-viewpoint demonstrations requires either a simulator with known camera control (unavailable for deployed hardware) or extensive human teleoperation across camera configurations — precisely the setting that motivates single-view imitation learning. Third, data augmentation must be repeated for each new deployment scenario as the camera setup changes, whereas an architectural bottleneck (VQ discretization) provides a deploy-once solution that generalizes structurally to arbitrary novel viewpoints without retraining. Concurrent work CKT-WAM (arXiv:2605.06247, May 2026) achieves 77.4% camera on LIBERO-Plus via parameter-efficient teacher-to-student knowledge transfer (DreamZero-14B teacher → Cosmos-Policy-2B student; 1.17% trainable parameters; teacher not required at inference), without targeting camera invariance specifically — camera robustness emerges as a byproduct of general WAM knowledge transfer rather than an architectural inductive bias, and CKT-WAM does not analyze the joint-attention camera failure mode. 77.4% is below OA-WAM's 80.5% single-camera architectural SOTA, establishing that general knowledge transfer without camera-specific design does not reach the current architectural ceiling. VQ-Perceiver thus targets a strictly harder and more deployment-realistic problem: achieving camera robustness via inductive bias from hard VQ discretization, using only the single-view demonstrations that practitioners actually collect, without knowledge of the test camera distribution. The primary comparisons are OA-WAM (80.5%, continuous slot attention, current single-camera architectural SOTA on LIBERO-Plus camera axis) and CKT-WAM (77.4%, teacher-student knowledge transfer, below OA-WAM), with VQ hard discretization as the differentiating mechanism against both; the 92.8% dual-camera ceiling is cited as broader context for what is achievable with additional hardware, not as a directly comparable single-camera target.\n\nThe information-bottleneck argument is precisely grounded: camera viewpoint changes alter pixel-level spatial arrangements but leave object identity, task phase, and gripper-object relationships invariant. However, the viewpoint-invariance claim is explicitly framed as an empirical hypothesis, not a guarantee. A K=512 codebook could in principle still encode viewpoint-specific routing if the Perceiver cross-attention queries learn viewpoint-dependent attention patterns. The task-action gradient pressure is the claimed mechanism that discourages this: viewpoint-specific features that do not improve action prediction should be suppressed by task-loss SGD. This hypothesis is directly tested by the UMAP codebook visualization: if codebook clusters organize by task phase and object identity rather than camera angle, the hypothesis is confirmed; if clusters organize by camera angle, the paper pivots to analyzing why discretization does or does not produce viewpoint invariance — still publishable as an analysis contribution with the UMAP evidence and quantified ablation. This requires no camera pose annotations, no multi-view demonstrations, and no test-time knowledge of the camera transformation. Sensor noise robustness is also expected to improve because VQ quantization is inherently denoising: perturbed continuous features map to the same code as their clean counterparts when perturbation magnitude is smaller than nearest-neighbor codebook decision boundaries, directly addressing the 43.1% noise score. The primary contribution framing targets: (a) improving over Motus's baseline on LIBERO-Plus camera axis, approaching or exceeding OA-WAM's architectural SOTA of 80.5% (arXiv:2605.06481, Table 2) using only single-view demonstrations, and contextualizing against the 92.8% data-augmentation ceiling; (b) citing the 65pp RoboTwin 2.0-Plus camera gap (21.6%) as published motivation, with secondary evaluation on RoboTwin 2.0-Plus if author code is obtained or Appendix A re-implementation is feasible within timeline. Motus vanilla baseline numbers are already published for RoboTwin 2.0-Plus (camera: 21.6%), saving that baseline run. Motus LIBERO-Plus baseline must be run once (~4h wall clock on 4 H100s). LIBERO-PLUS BASELINE CONTINGENCY: Three mutually exclusive contribution framings are prepared and deployed based on the day 1–2 baseline run result, before any fine-tuning begins. (A) If Motus LIBERO-Plus camera ≤55%: 'Closing a large gap (X% → Y%), substantially exceeding OA-WAM's architectural SOTA (80.5%) and approaching the data-augmentation ceiling (92.8%) — without any camera-augmented training data or knowledge of the test camera distribution' — strongest framing, directly analogous to the RoboTwin 2.0-Plus 65pp motivation gap; abstract and introduction proceed as currently drafted with gap-closing narrative. This scenario is also consistent with the RoboTwin 2.0-Plus 21.6% data: if Motus's attention design is fundamentally camera-brittle, a low LIBERO-Plus baseline is plausible. (B) If Motus LIBERO-Plus camera 56–75%: 'Demonstrating that hard VQ intra-routing achieves camera robustness comparable to or exceeding OA-WAM's architectural SOTA (80.5%), using only single-view demonstrations and requiring no camera pose information or augmented training data, with interpretable discrete codebook structure as an independent contribution' — method-comparison framing; abstract shifts from gap-closing to architectural comparison question (discrete vs. continuous routing for camera robustness); RoboTwin 2.0-Plus 21.6% still cited as published motivation for the general camera-fragility problem in joint-attention WAMs. (C) If Motus LIBERO-Plus camera >75%: Motus is already substantially camera-robust on LIBERO-Plus despite being fragile on RoboTwin 2.0-Plus, indicating the two benchmarks probe different viewpoint sensitivity axes; primary contribution pivots to VQ-Perceiver as an interpretable architectural alternative achieving comparable robustness to continuous slot approaches, with the UMAP codebook analysis, sensor noise improvement (VQ denoising from 43.1% noise baseline), and quantified discrete-vs-continuous routing ablation as primary contributions — the introduction acknowledges the LIBERO-Plus/RoboTwin 2.0-Plus benchmark divergence and repositions the problem around sensor noise and interpretability rather than camera gap-closing; narrower CoRL scope but publishable. Scenarios (A) and (B) are both strong CoRL contributions; (C) is a valid method paper with narrower scope. The 65pp RoboTwin 2.0-Plus gap provides corroborating motivation in (A) and (B); in (C) it is contextualized as benchmark-specific. Framing selection gates on day 1–2 baseline results and requires no architectural changes.",
  "landscape": "Motus (arXiv:2512.13030, TMLR 2025): Tri-model Joint Attention (concatenated self-attention across understanding, video, and action tokens); ~7B (WAN2.2-5B + Qwen3-VL-2B + action expert); public weights; confirmed camera viewpoint score 21.6% on RoboTwin 2.0-Plus (arXiv:2603.22078, Table 3); no published LIBERO-Plus results (absent from arXiv:2603.22078's LIBERO-Plus evaluation table — independently confirmed). ReViWo (proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/8882d370cdafec9885b918a8cfac642e, ICLR 2025): Representation learning for View-invariant World model; decomposes visual observations into VQ-coded view-invariant representation (VIR) + continuous view-dependent representation (VDR); trains a COMBO-based RL world model on VIR alone; achieves camera-robust manipulation on MetaWorld and PandaGym; real-world ALOHA experiments. Critical prior work establishing the VQ-for-viewpoint-invariance principle. Key limitations relative to this proposal: (a) requires labeled multi-view training data (known camera angles from MetaWorld simulator); (b) small-scale COMBO/RSSM world model, not a 7B diffusion MoT WAM; (c) offline VQ preprocessing step external to the policy, not intra-model routing; (d) model-based RL, not diffusion imitation learning. MotuBrain (arXiv:2604.27792, 2026): H-bridge design (middle 50% layers V-A joint attention, asymmetric at inference); no public pretrained checkpoint — excluded from scope. Fast-WAM (arXiv:2603.16666, 2026): skips video generation at test time for 4× speedup; targets efficiency only. GigaWorld-Policy (arXiv:2603.17240, 2026): causal decoupling for 9× speedup; efficiency only; no geometric robustness improvement. 'Do WAMs Generalize Better than VLAs?' (arXiv:2603.22078, 2026): benchmarks WAM robustness on RoboTwin 2.0-Plus and LIBERO-Plus; introduces RoboTwin 2.0-Plus, which adds seven explicit perturbation axes to RoboTwin 2.0, including camera viewpoint (altering the viewpoint pose of the third-person camera), robot initial configuration, language, lighting, background, sensor noise, and layout — camera viewpoint is absent from the original RoboTwin 2.0 domain-randomization axes; Cosmos-Policy reaches 82.2% overall on LIBERO-Plus and 75.8% on camera split; LingBot-VA: 28.9% camera on RoboTwin 2.0-Plus; Motus: 21.6% camera on RoboTwin 2.0-Plus — worst WAM camera score; Motus is NOT evaluated on LIBERO-Plus in this paper. CRITICAL AVAILABILITY NOTE: RoboTwin 2.0-Plus is an in-house Huawei/UToronto benchmark with no public evaluation code repository and no published camera perturbation parameter specification; the official RoboTwin 2.0 GitHub (github.com/RoboTwin-Platform/RoboTwin) does not include 2.0-Plus perturbation protocols; reproducing the evaluation requires either author-provided code (corresponding authors: Zhanguang Zhang / Yingxue Zhang at Huawei/UToronto) or re-implementation from Appendix A of arXiv:2603.22078. LIBERO-Plus (arXiv:2510.13626, ICLR 2026): fully public evaluation infrastructure (github.com/sylvestf/LIBERO-plus; dataset at huggingface.co/datasets/Sylvest/LIBERO-plus); drop-in replacement for LIBERO; 10,030 tasks across seven perturbation dimensions with 20,000+ trajectories; camera perturbation covers three sub-axes: C1 (distance 1.01×–2.00×), C2 (spherical position, Δθ/Δϕ within 15°–75° cones), C3 (orientation yaw/pitch/roll within 2°–10°); confirms camera viewpoint causes ~72pp average drop in VLAs; models show resilience to lighting and background; PRIMARY evaluation benchmark for this proposal. The LIBERO-Plus paper also demonstrates that fine-tuning OpenVLA-OFT on 20,000+ camera-augmented trajectories (with camera-view shifts within 5° of test camera positions) achieves 92.8% camera robustness — however, this result carries a material hardware confound: OpenVLA-OFT uses a dual-camera setup (external third-person + wrist camera), where the wrist-mounted camera provides stable close-range geometric cues invariant to external viewpoint changes (confirmed by the paper's own 'third-camera-blinded' ablation); Motus and VQ-Perceiver operate from a single external camera only, addressing a strictly harder single-camera setting; OpenVLA-OFT with dual cameras but without additional fine-tuning achieves only 56.4% camera on LIBERO-Plus. MWM (arXiv:2604.19683, 2026): predicts future semantic masks as geometric bottleneck; requires per-frame mask annotations; not applied to MoT WAMs. AnyCamVLA (arXiv:2603.05868, 2026): zero-shot camera viewpoint adaptation via feed-forward novel view synthesis at test time; plug-and-play for VLAs; requires knowing camera transformation at inference; training-free, not learned; not applicable to WAMs without adaptation; evaluated on custom LIBERO-based viewpoint benchmark (not LIBERO-Plus directly), achieving ~94.5% average under large perturbations. 'Dreaming the Unseen' (arXiv:2603.21017, 2026): continuous world-model regularization for OOD robustness; no discrete representations. Being-H0.7 (arXiv:2605.00078, 2026): K=16 latent reasoning queries as soft bottleneck; no VQ discretization — continuous queries can still encode viewpoint-specific features. Reports only aggregate LIBERO-Plus scores (82.1% zero-shot, 84.8% fine-tuned) without any camera-specific breakdown; the paper's claim of 'resilience against shifted viewpoints, novel textures, and sensor noise' is an umbrella inference from the aggregate score, not a disaggregated camera-axis measurement. Evaluated on RoboTwin 2.0 (not RoboTwin 2.0-Plus): clean 90.2%, domain-randomized (Hard) 89.6%; RoboTwin 2.0 domain randomization covers table-top clutter, varied lighting conditions, diverse background textures, tabletop height variations, and diverse language instructions — camera viewpoint/extrinsic perturbation is not among the RoboTwin 2.0 axes; accordingly, Being-H0.7's 89.6% domain-randomized score does not reflect camera-extrinsic robustness as measured by RoboTwin 2.0-Plus's dedicated camera split, and does not undermine the core problem statement. The proposed Perceiver-only ablation (N_ws=64 continuous queries, masking ON) is not architecturally matched to Being-H0.7's K=16 queries; it serves to isolate the contribution of hard VQ discretization at fixed N_ws=64, not to directly replicate Being-H0.7. ARRO (arXiv:2505.08627, 2026): zero-shot segmentation masking at inference; training-free; targets appearance, not camera viewpoint. VILA (arXiv:2601.02994, 2026): view-invariant latent actions (output action space); operates on action representations not visual tokens. GCQ (arXiv:2510.16039, 2025): action-conditioned VQ for spatiotemporal compression in recurrent world models; different target and mechanism. VQ-VLA (ICCV 2025): VQ on output action tokens, not visual representations. OA-WAM (arXiv:2605.06481, 2026): object-addressable cross-attention without discrete compression; trained on standard LIBERO demonstrations with LIBERO-Plus held out as out-of-distribution evaluation (no camera-augmented training data); camera score 80.5% on LIBERO-Plus (Table 2, arXiv:2605.06481v1 — current architectural SOTA on LIBERO-Plus camera axis among methods that do not use camera-augmented training data, exceeding Cosmos-Policy's 75.8% and π0.5's 75.4%); achieves SOTA on LIBERO-Plus geometric axes (geo avg 84.3%, overall avg 83.9%) via slot-based soft attention — important continuous-bottleneck baseline demonstrating camera robustness is achievable without VQ or augmented data; comparison against OA-WAM's continuous-slot approach vs. our hard VQ approach is a planned ablation. Note: Being-H0.7 reports a higher overall aggregate score (84.8% fine-tuned) than OA-WAM (83.9%), but does not publish a camera-axis breakdown; OA-WAM's 80.5% remains the only published reference for the LIBERO-Plus camera axis specifically among architecturally-motivated methods. The separate data-augmentation ceiling of 92.8% (OpenVLA-OFT fine-tuned on 20K+ camera-augmented trajectories, per LIBERO-Plus paper arXiv:2510.13626) is not directly comparable — it uses in-distribution camera augmentation calibrated to test positions, relies on a dual-camera hardware setup, and is not an architectural result. CKT-WAM (arXiv:2605.06247, May 2026): Parameter-efficient Context Knowledge Transfer between World Action Models; freezes both teacher (DreamZero-14B) and student (Cosmos-Policy-2B) WAMs; transfers teacher knowledge via compact text-space context vectors using learnable-query cross-attention (LQCA) compressors, an always-on generalized adapter, and sparsely activated specialized adapters — context is appended to the student's conditioning textual embeddings; teacher not required at inference (context precomputed). Trainable parameters: 1.17% of student model. LIBERO-Plus results (Table 1): camera 77.4%, robot 71.4%, language 86.7%, light 98.2%, background 90.2%, noise 94.8%, layout 88.5%, total 86.1%. Camera robustness emerges as a byproduct of general knowledge transfer from a larger frozen teacher WAM, not from targeted camera-invariance inductive bias; CKT-WAM does not analyze or specifically address the camera-specific failure mode in joint-attention WAMs and requires a separate large teacher WAM (DreamZero-14B). 77.4% camera is below OA-WAM's 80.5% single-camera architectural SOTA. VQ-Perceiver contrast: targets camera invariance via hard quantization within a single deployed WAM (no teacher required), with interpretable codebook UMAP analysis as empirical test of viewpoint-invariant organization; hard VQ prevents viewpoint-specific feature interpolation in a way that continuous knowledge-transfer context vectors cannot guarantee. GeoAware-VLA (arXiv:2509.14117, 2025): implicit geometry-aware VLA; evaluates on standard LIBERO novel-view protocol (not LIBERO-Plus), reporting ~82.6% on novel camera views for GeoAware-BAKU vs. 37.9% for standard BAKU — different benchmark from LIBERO-Plus, not directly comparable. X-WAM (arXiv:2604.26694, 2026): Unified 4D World Action Modeling via asynchronous denoising; predicts multi-view RGB-D videos; requires multi-view training data; continuous representations; targets 4D reconstruction and efficiency, not single-view viewpoint invariance; orthogonal. XR-1/UVMC (arXiv:2511.02776, ICLR 2026): dual-branch VQ-VAE with vision branch and motion branch aligned via KL-divergence; offline preprocessing step before model inference, not intra-model routing; targets cross-embodiment generalization via shared codebook, not geometric viewpoint robustness within a running WAM. DIAL (arXiv:2603.29844, 2026): continuous latent visual foresight as structural bottleneck between System-2 (VLM reasoning) and System-1 (action decoder); targets intent decoupling and training instability in VLAs; continuous representations (not discrete); different model type (VLA, not WAM) and different failure mode (training instability, not camera viewpoint brittleness). 'Do You Know Where Your Camera Is? View-Invariant Policy Learning with Camera Conditioning' (arXiv:2510.02268, 2025): conditions ACT, Diffusion Policy, and SmolVLA on Plücker embeddings of camera extrinsics; significantly improves viewpoint generalization; requires known camera extrinsics at both training and test time; no VQ; not applicable to WAMs; orthogonal approach (explicit extrinsic conditioning vs. learned discrete bottleneck requiring no camera pose). No concurrent work extends intra-model VQ discretization of visual token representations within a deployed diffusion-based MoT WAM to address camera viewpoint robustness without multi-view training data.",
  "approach": "All experiments use the public Motus checkpoint (~7B: WAN2.2-5B + Qwen3-VL-2B + action expert; motus-robotics/Motus, HuggingFace). The modification has three components: (1) VQ-Perceiver module: N_ws=64 randomly-initialized learnable world-state query vectors perform multi-head cross-attention over the N_video≈256 video tokens output by Motus's video VAE. The N_ws cross-attended outputs are quantized via straight-through VQ-VAE to a jointly-trained codebook of K=512 entries with EMA updates and commitment loss weight λ_vq ramped from 0.01 to 0.25 over the first 5K steps (ramp prevents large commitment gradients from driving codebook collapse before the cross-attention pathway is established). Result: N_ws=64 discrete world-state tokens. (2) Action routing in Motus joint attention: apply an attention mask in Motus's Tri-model Joint Attention so that action tokens cannot directly attend to raw video tokens (action←video path blocked). Video tokens retain full joint attention with understanding tokens and other video tokens; video tokens can still attend to action tokens (preserving action-conditioned video generation). (3) Discrete world-state cross-attention: a dedicated cross-attention sublayer added after each joint attention block allows action tokens to attend exclusively to the N_ws=64 VQ-quantized world-state tokens. Fine-tuning protocol: LoRA (rank=64) applied to all joint attention and new cross-attention layers; VQ-Perceiver initialized randomly; 30K steps on LIBERO + RoboTwin 2.0 demonstrations; combined objective: action rectified-flow diffusion loss + VQ commitment loss. Warm-up schedule: attention masking probability ramped from 0 to 1 over first 5K steps to avoid instability. Training stability monitoring: adding a randomly initialized VQ-Perceiver to a pretrained 7B system risks initialization mismatch — action tokens may find the new cross-attention pathway uninformative relative to the blocked direct video route, resulting in near-zero gradients to the VQ-Perceiver in early training. Two mitigations are added: (a) codebook gradient norm monitoring from step 500 — if VQ-Perceiver cross-attention layer gradient norm is below 10% of the joint attention layer gradient norm at step 2K, the attention masking warm-up is extended from 5K to 10K steps, giving the pathway more time to establish useful routing before full masking is applied; (b) the λ_vq ramp described above. These triggers are implemented as automated training callbacks. PRIMARY evaluation: LIBERO-Plus (github.com/sylvestf/LIBERO-plus; dataset: huggingface.co/datasets/Sylvest/LIBERO-plus) — fully public benchmark with defined camera perturbation protocol (C1/C2/C3 axes, 15°–75° spherical cones). Run Motus LIBERO-Plus baseline first (~4h wall clock on 4 H100s, day 1–2) to establish comparison point and select framing variant (see LIBERO-PLUS BASELINE CONTINGENCY in opportunity section); current camera-axis SOTA among architecturally-motivated methods trained without camera-augmented demonstrations is OA-WAM at 80.5% (arXiv:2605.06481, Table 2); the LIBERO-Plus benchmark paper (arXiv:2510.13626) additionally shows that OpenVLA-OFT fine-tuned on 20K+ camera-augmented trajectories reaches 92.8% — a data-augmentation ceiling against which VQ-Perceiver is contextualized but not directly compared (VQ-Perceiver targets structural invariance without augmented training data). FULL EVALUATION TABLE: Report the complete LIBERO-Plus evaluation table across all 7 perturbation axes — camera (C1/C2/C3 combined), lighting, background, sensor noise, layout, robot initial state, and language instruction — for three models: (1) Motus-vanilla baseline, (2) VQ-Perceiver K=512/N_ws=64/masking ON (main method), (3) Perceiver-only N_ws=64 continuous queries/masking ON (VQ ablation). Primary scientific claim is camera-axis improvement. Secondary analysis explicitly documents whether the K=512 VQ bottleneck preserves, improves, or regresses on appearance axes (lighting, background) where Motus currently performs well on RoboTwin 2.0-Plus (~84–85%): regression would indicate information-compression loss from the bottleneck, which is reported transparently and analyzed as a capacity-invariance tradeoff. Full-table reporting is required to rule out cherry-picking and provides CoRL reviewers with complete empirical characterization of the bottleneck's effect across all perturbation types. SECONDARY evaluation: RoboTwin 2.0-Plus — Motus vanilla baseline 21.6% taken from arXiv:2603.22078 Table 3 (no baseline run required). CRITICAL DEPENDENCY: RoboTwin 2.0-Plus evaluation code is NOT publicly available (in-house Huawei/UToronto benchmark from arXiv:2603.22078; no GitHub repo or perturbation parameter specification released). Contingency protocol: (a) Contact corresponding authors Zhanguang Zhang / Yingxue Zhang (Huawei/UToronto) within day 1–2 of project start to request evaluation code or environment snapshot; (b) if code is not obtainable within 2 days, implement RoboTwin 2.0-Plus camera perturbation from Appendix A of arXiv:2603.22078 by adapting LIBERO-Plus's C2 spherical-position protocol to the RoboTwin 2.0 Aloha-Agilex bimanual simulator — estimated 1–2 days of implementation work; (c) if neither is feasible within the CoRL timeline, the paper reports LIBERO-Plus as sole primary evaluation and cites the 21.6% RoboTwin 2.0-Plus score exclusively as published motivation in the introduction. CoRL scope (3 fine-tuning runs): (a) VQ-Perceiver K=512, N_ws=64, attention masking ON (main method); (b) Perceiver-only (continuous soft queries N_ws=64, no VQ, masking ON — ablates discretization; isolates the contribution of hard VQ over continuous routing at fixed N_ws=64; note this uses N_ws=64 continuous queries and is not architecturally matched to Being-H0.7's K=16 latent reasoning queries, so it does not constitute a direct replication of Being-H0.7 — the primary goal is to quantify whether VQ discretization per se improves camera robustness); (c) VQ-Perceiver K=512, N_ws=64, masking OFF (VQ as auxiliary path — ablates routing). ICLR fallback ablations (add 3 more runs): K∈{128,1024}; N_ws∈{16,128}; FSQ variant. Interpretability: UMAP visualization of codebook assignments colored by (i) camera angle, (ii) task phase, (iii) object identity, to verify camera-angle-invariant semantic organization — this is the primary empirical test of the viewpoint-invariance hypothesis. Codebook utilization monitoring from step 500 onward; EMA restart if per-code usage below 1/K² threshold by step 2K.",

ViPRA (Video Prediction for Robot Actions) is a pretraining-finetuning framework that converts video prediction models into robot control policies, enabling learning from unlabeled videos without requiring explicit action annotations.

The method addresses a fundamental limitation in robot learning: "Videos, including those of humans or teleoperated robots, capture rich physical interactions. However, most of them lack labeled actions," restricting their utility for policy training.

## Core Method

Rather than predicting actions directly, ViPRA employs a two-stage approach:

1. **Pretraining phase**: A video-language model learns to predict both future visual observations and "motion-centric latent actions, which serve as intermediate representations of scene dynamics." These latent actions are trained using perceptual losses and optical flow consistency.

2. **Finetuning phase**: A "chunked flow matching decoder" maps learned latent actions to robot-specific continuous action sequences using only 100-200 teleoperated demonstrations.

## VQ-VAE Usage

The document does not mention VQ-VAE. The method instead emphasizes optical flow consistency and perceptual losses for training latent action representations.

The framework builds on a video-language model foundation, though specific architectural details aren't provided in this abstract.

# VQ-VAE Usage in ViPRA

## Input and Encoding

VQ-VAE in ViPRA serves **two distinct purposes**:

1. **Visual Tokenization**: The frozen VQ-VAE encoder from LWM (the base video-language model) converts visual observations into discrete visual tokens for the pretraining phase.

2. **Latent Action Learning**: A separate VQ-VAE architecture with quantization extracts motion-centric latent actions from video frames during the first training phase.

## Separate Processing

The two applications operate **independently**:
- Visual tokens come from the pretrained LWM's VQ-VAE (kept frozen)
- Latent action tokens are learned through a custom inverse dynamics encoder and forward decoder pipeline using vector quantization with a shared codebook

## Codebook Details

The latent action codebook has a fixed size of 8 with 32-dimensional embeddings. The paper employs "Noise-Substitution Vector Quantization (NSVQ)" rather than standard straight-through estimation, enabling gradient flow without auxiliary codebook losses.

## Core Objectives

ViPRA's primary goals are:
- Learning robot control policies from **unlabeled human and robot videos**
- Enabling "smooth, high-frequency continuous control" for manipulation tasks
- Achieving data efficiency through pretraining-finetuning with only hundreds of teleoperated demonstrations

## Architecture & Benchmarks

Built on **LWM-Chat-1M** (a video-language foundation model), ViPRA evaluates on SIMPLER benchmark and real-world robotic tasks, demonstrating 16% improvements over strong baselines.
